newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian conglomerates slump in stock market.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian conglomerates slump in stock market.

text.p: Nigerian conglomerates were big losers in Wednesday's bearish stock trading, dealers said.
The key sector witnessed sizeable price drops which caused the all-share index to fall to 8660.57 from 8683.28 on Tuesday.
Dealers said conglomerates were joined by banking and brewery shares in the current selling mood that has left no sacred cows.

"The market is responding to the interplay of forces of demand and supply more than ever before," one trader said. "Blue chips which until recently were considered untouchable are now on offer and we don't know for how long."
Analysts said reluctance on the part of investors was responsible for the trend after many stocks had risen significantly earlier in the year.
Lever Brothers and John Holt led losers with 10 kobo losses to 28.70 naira and 9.60 naira, respectively.
PZ Industries, the market's most capitalised firm, closed five kobo down at 29.70 naira.
Nigerian Breweries was the heaviest casualty, sliding one naira to 20.20 naira as dealers spoke of large quantities on offer.
High street banks First Bank and Union Bank finished at 14.80 naira and 14.70 naira, respectively, shedding 20 kobo apiece.
Food giant Nestle meanwhile maintained its upswing, adding 1.88 naira to hit 85.08 naira.
Construction firm G. Cappa followed, closing one naira up at 15.00 naira.
Increasing demand for the stocks was responsible for the big gains, said dealers.
Texaco rose five kobo to 39.05 naira but Agip fell by the same margin to close at 22.85 naira.
